1d2f3788e6.q: What is Eve OS and how does it expand Eve's capabilities for law firms?
1d2f3788e6.a: Eve OS is the evolution of Eve that enables attorneys and law firms to serve more clients than ever before. The platform now includes AI agents that can run tasks, field intake calls, conduct outbound calls with voice AI, and take browser actions to automate civil chair activities like logging into systems and working with RCMS and DMS. Eve can read documents, pull information automatically, write back to your CMS, and provide intelligence across the entire case lifecycle to identify missed opportunities like mass torts or TBI claims.

2923f8eaee.q: How does Eve's AI improve intake call handling and lead scoring for plaintiff law firms?
2923f8eaee.a: Eve provides live call coaching to keep staff up to date on tactics across the board. The AI can suggest real-time coaching during calls—for example, prompting an intake specialist to dig deeper with a client question. Eve also provides lead scoring so that callers don't miss any transcript or proper case evaluation, ensuring nothing moves to the next stage improperly. The adoption of these features has been strong, with after-hours and overflow intake activity being the largest piece of adoption today.

0763569a33.q: Why is zero data retention critical for Eve and how does it differ from consumer AI tools?
0763569a33.a: Zero data retention is critical for the legal industry because many consumer AI accounts allow data sharing, especially through thumbs up feedback, which would allow model providers to obtain attorney data—a no-go for legal practice. Eve raised this concern multiple times with Anthropic and OpenAI, noting that while cheaper consumer accounts enable data trading, legal firms cannot allow their confidential data to be shared. Eve works technically with AI providers to ensure data is not retained inappropriately, even when safety evaluation is required.

989e36204e.q: How is Eve positioned against major tech companies entering the legal AI space?
989e36204e.a: Eve sees the legal market splitting into two sections: software for institutions like big law and companies, and software for people—plaintiff law firms. Eve is currently the main player serving plaintiff firms at scale, whereas OpenAI and large companies focus primarily on enterprise and in-house use. Eve's advantage is in proving utility to law firm owners who built their businesses over 20 years, whereas large companies with unlimited budgets for experiments can afford different approaches.
